findings.title: Target's nested objects lose their null members
findings.why: The target's members are copied with `merge(undefined, target[key])`. That call treats the value as a patch and deletes `null` members. With target `{"a":{"x":null,"y":1}}` and patch `{"b":1}`, the result is `{"a":{"y":1},"b":1}`. RFC 7386 and the spec require `{"a":{"x":null,"y":1},"b":1}`, so stored data is silently lost. The test at line 18 of `test/json-merge-patch.test.ts` only covers a top-level null, so it misses this.

findings.title: Arrays in the patch have nulls stripped from their objects
findings.why: Array items are copied with `merge(undefined, item)`. That strips `null` members from any object inside the array. With patch `{"a":[{"b":null}]}`, the result is `{"a":[{}]}`. The spec says arrays are replaced whole and a non-object patch gives a copy of it, so the result should be `{"a":[{"b":null}]}`.
